case_title: Balu Sudam Khalde & Anr. v. State of Maharashtra
accused_victim_relationship: Not stated; the only connection described is a verbal altercation between appellant No. 2 and the deceased on the night of the incident, with no prior relationship or enmity described.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 r/w s.34 (convicted); IPC s.323, s.324 and s.504, each r/w s.34, were also charged (accused Nos. 1-4)
evidence_type: Eyewitness (three witnesses), medical (post-mortem), recovery (discovery panchnamas of weapons), res gestae statement
confession: None relied on. Police-custody statements leading to weapon discovery are noted in the facts but the Court did not rely on them.
aggravating_circumstances: Nine blows with a dangerous weapon (sickle and sword) on an unarmed, helpless victim; injuries on vital parts of the body
mitigating_circumstances: None accepted by the Court. Defence argued sudden fight and heat of passion (Exception 4), but the Court assumed it only for argument and rejected it.
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 r/w s.34 IPC; life imprisonment and Rs. 1000 fine each (default six months RI); accused Nos. 2 and 4 acquitted
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed (CRLA No. 637 of 2003); conviction and sentence affirmed
neutral_facts: Late on the night of the incident, the victim was talking with a friend near a car consultancy shop in a slum area when one of the accused passing by approached him, and a verbal exchange followed. Shortly afterwards, the accused arrived with others and a fight broke out. The victim's friend was struck on the head with a sickle and a sword and was bleeding. The victim was then severely attacked with a sickle and a sword, receiving multiple wounds to the hands, wrist, arm, shoulder and chest. A neighbour came out of his house during the assault and asked what the fighting was about. The injured friend asked a rickshaw driver known to them to watch the victim and then went with a neighbour to the police station to report the incident. Police took the victim to hospital, where he was declared dead. The post-mortem examination found multiple injuries, including a stab wound to the right chest that cut the ribs and entered the lung. The doctor opined that this injury was sufficient in the ordinary course to cause death, and that the injuries were caused by sharp-edged weapons. Three eyewitnesses gave oral evidence, including the injured friend, the neighbour and the rickshaw driver. The rickshaw driver stated that the injured friend told him what had happened. Following statements made by the accused in police custody, weapons were recovered in the presence of panch witnesses. A chargesheet was filed after investigation.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from multiple sickle and sword injuries (nine injuries, including a stab wound to the right chest cutting ribs and lung); injured friend suffered a bleeding head injury
number_of_offences: 4 charged (ss.302, 323, 324, 504, each r/w s.34); 1 finally upheld (s.302 r/w s.34)
premeditation_planning: Not found by the Court; premeditation was not decided and the sudden-fight assumption was made only for argument
motive: alleged: verbal altercation between appellant No. 2 and the deceased that escalated into a fight
key_evidence_accepted: Consistent ocular evidence of PW 1, PW 2 and PW 3; cross-examination suggestions establishing PW 1's presence and the assault; PW 3's res gestae account of what PW 1 told him (ss.6 and 7 Evidence Act); post-mortem evidence of PW 7 on the nature of injuries
witness_credibility: Found reliable; concurrent findings of the trial court and High Court upheld; the Court saw no good reason to disbelieve the three eyewitnesses
post_offence_conduct: Accused allegedly offered in police custody to show where the sickle and sword were concealed; discovery panchnamas were drawn. The Court did not rely on this as a finding.
bail_history: Both appellants released on bail during the pendency of the appeal (appellant No. 2 on 01.10.2010; appellant No. 1 on 04.03.2013)
trial_duration: offence: 01.04.2001; trial judgment: 12.03.2003; High Court: 02.03.2009; Supreme Court: March 29, 2023
legal_representation: Appellants: K. L. Janjani, Pankaj Kumar Singh, Dr. Vinod Kumar Tewari, Kailash J. Kashyap. State: Abhikalp Pratap Singh, Siddharth Dharmadhikari, Aadityaa Aniruddha Pande, Bharat Bagla, Sourav Singh, Ms. Shreya Saxena, Ms. Yamini Singh
investigation_status: FIR lodged by PW 1; scene and inquest panchnamas drawn; post-mortem conducted; weapons recovered on discovery panchnamas; chargesheet filed; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: None noted by the Supreme Court. The High Court noted the absence of a medical certificate for the injuries to PW 1 and PW 2, which the Supreme Court did not treat as a procedural lapse.
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted s.302 r/w s.34 (life), acquitted A2 and A4. High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction and sentence affirmed. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed.
prosecution_argument: No good reason to doubt the eyewitnesses or for them to falsely implicate the appellants; Exception 4 not made out given nine injuries by sickle and sword; discovery of weapons is conduct evidence under s.8 supporting the ocular version
defence_argument: Eyewitness evidence unreliable; PW 1's presence doubtful with no medical treatment or certificate; discovery panchnama unreliable as panch witnesses did not support it; case falls under Exception 4 to s.300, alternatively s.304 Part I
legal_principle_applied: Appreciation of ocular evidence (two-part test on presence and inherent improbability); concurrent findings interfered with only in exceptional cases; defence suggestions and replies may be relied on; s.6 res gestae; Exception 4 requires all four ingredients; s.300 thirdly applied
precedent_relied_upon: Bharwada Bhoginbhai Hirjibhai v. State of Gujarat (AIR 1983 SC 753); Leela Ram v. State of Haryana (AIR 1995 SC 3717); Tahsildar Singh v. State of UP (AIR 1959 SC 1012); Tarun Bora v. State of Assam (2002 Cri LJ 4076); Rakesh Kumar v. State of Haryana (1987) 2 SCC 34; Rajwant Singh v. State of Kerala (AIR 1966 SC 1874); State of AP v. Rayavarapu Punnayya (1976) 4 SCC 382; Sukhar v. State of UP (1999) 9 SCC 507; Govind s/o Soneram v. State of MP (2005 Cri LJ 1244); Parkash Chand v. State of HP (2004) 11 SCC 381
judicial_aggravating_factors: Nine blows with a dangerous weapon on an unarmed, helpless victim; injuries to vital parts of the body by sickle and sword
other_sentence_order: Bail bonds cancelled; appellants to surrender within two weeks and be sent to judicial custody to serve the sentence imposed
